newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea May trade deficit narrows to $686 mln.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea May trade deficit narrows to $686 mln.

text.p: South Korea's customs-cleared trade deficit narrowed sharply to $686 million in May from a $1.44 billion shortfall a year earlier, provisional figures released by the trade ministry showed on Monday.
May Apr May 96
Trade balance -686 -1,486 -1,443
NOTE: in millions of dollars, April figures revised
South Korea's customs-cleared trade deficit totalled $9.56 billion in the first five months of this year, up from $7.65 billion in the same 1996 period, the ministry figures showed.
The ministry said in a statement FOB exports rose 3.9 percent in May year-on-year, while CIF imports fell 2.5 percent.
The May exports growth marked the second straight monthly rise for 1997. Exports posted negative growth in the January to March period.
The monthly deficit also shrank from a shortfall of $1.49 billion in April, the figures showed.
Semiconductor exports gained 8.8 percent in May, the first year-on-year rise in 13 months, it said.
"It appears the semiconductor export problem, which has been the major factor behind the ballooning trade deficit, has eased to some extent," the ministry said.
On the other hand, exports excluding semiconductors rose 3.2 percent. But the ministry said the growth was slower than a 9.6 percent rise in April.
"A rise in export growth has continued in heavy industrial and chemical products sectors such as automobiles, steel products and petrochemical goods," the ministry said.
"But the growth in light industrial exports such as shoes, textile products, toys, dolls, plastic goods, leather and fur products, has slowed," it said.
The ministry said May's decline in imports was the first such drop in the past eight months.
The ministry said slowing crude import and a slowdown in capital and consumer goods purchases were responsible for the overall decline in imports.
"The ministry forecasts the current trade deficit to continue improving in the absence of any dramatic changes in domestic and international markets," it said.
The trade ministry earlier forecast a $14 billion trade deficit this year against a $20.62 billion shortfall in 1996.
